lines.before: A standing grant (A27, the owner, 2026-10-31) lets named outward acts run without a yes per act. **What it holds:** `.kit/autonomy.json` names each act (for example push to main, tag, release, merge, delete a merged branch, message running sessions about a release) and the conditions it must pass. Only the owner writes or changes it; a change to it, to `.claude/autonomy.mjs` or to a gate it runs is never granted. **Before each act:** `node .claude/autonomy.mjs check <act>` reads the grant from the remote's main, never the working copy, and runs the evidence itself (tests, scrub, caps, the new test failing before the fix); a failed, missing or unreadable condition means ask the owner. **Kill switch:** the file `autonomy-off` in the Claude config folder, outside every repo; while it exists every act asks. **After:** each granted act is one line in `reports/autopilot/log.md` with its proof (the SHA or URL read back from the remote) and is reported to the owner. **Never granted:** changing the grant or its gates, deleting user data, public posts, Tier 0 rule text, or anything a test or the sweep did not pass. Projects ship with no grant (A27 `none`), so every act asks; until `autonomy.mjs` exists, no grant is in force (plan kit-autopilot). Why: the owner sets the conditions once and hears after with proof, and a gate the session can edit is no gate.
lines.after: A standing grant (A27, the owner, 2026-10-31) lets named outward acts run without a yes per act. **What it holds:** `.kit/autonomy.json` names each act (for example push to main, tag, release, merge, delete a merged branch, message running sessions about a release) and the conditions it must pass. Only the owner writes or changes it; a change to it, to `.claude/autonomy.mjs` or to a gate it runs is never granted. **Before each act:** `node .claude/autonomy.mjs check <act>` reads the grant from the remote's main, never the working copy, and runs the evidence itself (tests, scrub, caps, the new test failing before the fix); a failed, missing or unreadable condition means ask the owner. **Kill switch:** the file `autonomy-off` in the Claude config folder, outside every repo; while it exists every act asks. **After:** each granted act is one line in `reports/autopilot/log.md` with its proof (the SHA or URL read back from the remote) and is reported to the owner. **Never granted:** changing the grant or its gates, deleting user data, public posts, Tier 0 rule text, or anything a test or the sweep did not pass. **No act skips a prompt:** the ledger is advisory, and only the owner can change that, when an act first reaches 10 straight hits. Projects ship with no grant (A27 `none`), so every act asks; even a project with a grant asks while the ledger is advisory (plan kit-autopilot). Why: the owner sets the conditions once and hears after with proof, and a gate the session can edit is no gate, nor is a verdict it can write.
lines.why: the owner, 2026-10-31: the streak of owner verdicts is advisory (the ledger is forgeable), so no act skips a prompt, and only the owner can change that when an act first reaches 10 straight hits

lines.before: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **Two passes:** one large sweep, then ONE short re-sweep over the whole batch (by tier: rule:sweep-tiers) (never per fix - an undamped loop) of whether the fixes broke anything; a third only for a major re-sweep finding.
lines.after: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **Two passes:** one large sweep, then ONE short re-sweep over the whole batch (by tier: rule:sweep-tiers) (never per fix - an undamped loop) of whether the fixes broke anything; no third: high and above fixed now, the rest next-session clean-up.
lines.why: the owner's sweep loop: one re-sweep, no third; its high and above fixed now, the rest next-session clean-up (IR-2026-10-31-sweep-loop-auto-approved-contract-fix-auto-approved-targeted)

lines.before: **Value check:** tier remaining work by what a user would notice (high: someone hits it; medium: keyboard or screen-reader correctness; low: millisecond races, byte trims, test hygiene), say the tier at each checkpoint, and recommend stopping when reviews return ever smaller things, before the owner asks; the value lens ends the loop, not fatigue. Why: a sweep generates work faster than value.

lines.before: A feature, fix or triage sweep's Swarm Contract is approved by `approve.mjs`, never an agent: same contract, same answer. It runs first: an approval prints the owner's notice; only an ASK goes to the owner (yes logged, `--owner-yes`); a hook holds reviewers until the log clears this HEAD and contract. It approves only when the tier's and modifiers' roles are there, each with its own question, context, finding shape and budget, within the tier's caps; else the owner decides, told why. First push and launch gate always go to the owner. Each decision and outcome is logged; it pauses after tokens 25% over budget, a third of findings repeated, a bug escaping a passed sweep, or every 10 approvals (the trial review; 20 after two clean in a row, 10 again after any other pause), and only the owner resumes it. Why: a routine sweep need not wait; the log shows when it drifts.
lines.after: A feature, fix or triage sweep's Swarm Contract is approved by `approve.mjs`, never an agent: same contract, same answer. It runs first: an approval prints the owner's notice; only an ASK goes to the owner (yes logged, `--owner-yes`); a hook holds reviewers until the log clears this HEAD and contract. It approves only when the tier's and modifiers' roles are there, each with its own question, context, finding shape and budget, within the tier's caps; else the owner decides, told why. First push and launch gate always go to the owner. A re-sweep (`--resweep`) instead needs a role naming each file its fixes changed. Each decision and outcome is logged; it pauses after tokens 25% over budget, a third of findings repeated, a bug escaping a passed sweep, or every 10 approvals (the trial review; 20 after two clean in a row, 10 again after any other pause), and only the owner resumes it. Why: a routine sweep need not wait; the log shows when it drifts.
lines.why: approve.mjs --resweep approves the one re-sweep by its own floor (IR-2026-10-31-sweep-loop-auto-approved-contract-fix-auto-approved-targeted)

lines.before: **Who tests the preview, by stakes.** Every user-facing PR: the lead checks the deployed preview in phone and desktop emulation (headers, security policy, workers, layout), shown as shots. The owner's real device only for: a new or often-used surface; touch, keyboard or installed-app behaviour; device-only paths (downloads, file imports, sharing); screen-reader checks. Why: emulation cannot prove a device's fonts, system UI, keyboard or storage, so the owner's time goes where only a hand can tell.
